nguy-n-dynasty.name: Nguyễn dynasty
nguy-n-dynasty.summary: The last Vietnamese dynasty, ruling unified Vietnam from 1802 until the French protectorate began in 1883, and nominally until 1945 when the last emperor abolished the treaty with France.

minh-m-ng.name: Minh Mạng
minh-m-ng.summary: Second emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty (r. 1820–1841), known for opposing French influence, conquering Champa, briefly annexing Cambodia and enforcing strict Confucian orthodoxy.

peranakan-chinese.name: Peranakan Chinese
peranakan-chinese.summary: An ethnic group descended from early Chinese settlers in Southeast Asian ports such as Malacca and Singapore, whose culture blends Chinese and local traditions.

nguy-n-nh-chi-u.name: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
nguy-n-nh-chi-u.summary: Vietnamese poet (1822–1888) known for nationalist, anti-colonial writing against French rule in Cochinchina, celebrated in the south for defying the treaty ceding the region to France.

stamford-raffles.name: Stamford Raffles
stamford-raffles.summary: British colonial official (1781–1826) who served as governor of the Dutch East Indies and secured Singapore for Britain in 1819, also writing The History of Java.

hokkien.name: Hokkien
hokkien.summary: A variety of Chinese from the Southern Min branch, native to southern Fujian and Taiwan, historically the lingua franca among overseas Chinese traders in maritime Southeast Asia.

first-anglo-burmese-war.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
first-anglo-burmese-war.summary: War fought 1824–1826 between the British and Burmese empires, ending in a costly but decisive British victory that gave Britain control of Assam and other regions.

gustave-eiffel.name: Gustave Eiffel
gustave-eiffel.summary: French civil engineer (1832–1923) known for railway bridges, the Eiffel Tower and his contribution to the Statue of Liberty; later researched meteorology and aerodynamics.

paul-doumer.name: Paul Doumer
paul-doumer.summary: French politician who served as President of France from 1931 until his assassination in 1932, known as 'the Father of French Indochina' for his work as its governor general.

bamboo-organ.name: Bamboo Organ
bamboo-organ.summary: A 19th-century church organ in Las Piñas, Philippines, completed in 1824 with 902 of its 1,031 pipes made of bamboo; restored in Germany in the 1970s and now a National Cultural Treasure.

shophouse.name: Shophouse
shophouse.summary: A building type combining a shop and residence, common in Southeast Asia and parts of South China, Hong Kong, Macau and Sri Lanka, typically built in terraced rows with arcades.

spoliarium.name: Spoliarium
spoliarium.summary: A painting by Filipino artist Juan Luna depicting dying gladiators, which won a gold medal at Madrid's 1884 national art exposition.

san-sebastian-church-manila.name: San Sebastian Church
san-sebastian-church-manila.summary: Basilica in Manila completed in 1891, notable as the only all-steel church building in the Philippines.

c-c-river.name: Cổ Cò River
c-c-river.summary: A partially silted river near Da Nang, Vietnam, that from the 16th to 18th century was a key shipping lane linking the ports of Hội An and Da Nang before it became too silted for use.

ilocano-people.name: Ilocano people
ilocano-people.summary: An Austronesian ethnolinguistic group native to the Ilocos Region of northwestern Luzon in the Philippines, now the country's third-largest ethnic group.

british-rule-in-burma.name: British Burma
british-rule-in-burma.summary: Period of British colonial control over Burma from 1824 to 1948, established through three Anglo-Burmese Wars and at times administered as a province of British India.

french-indochina.name: French Indochina
french-indochina.summary: A federation of French-ruled territories in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, that existed from 1887 to 1954, with capitals at Hanoi and Saigon.

da-nang.name: Da Nang
da-nang.summary: Vietnam's fourth-largest city, known as Tourane under French colonial rule (1884–1945) and earlier as Cửa Hàn; today a transport hub on the South Central Coast.

t-c.name: Tự Đức
t-c.summary: Fourth emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty and the country's last pre-colonial monarch, ruling for about 36 years from 1847 to 1883.

cochinchina.name: Cochinchina
cochinchina.summary: Historical name for southern Vietnam, originally the Đàng Trong domain of the Nguyễn lords in the 17th-18th centuries, later a French colony from the 1860s.

tonkin.name: Tonkin
tonkin.summary: A historical name for the Red River Delta region of northern Vietnam, later used for the French colonial protectorate there from 1883 to 1945.

anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824
anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824.summary: A treaty signed between the United Kingdom and the Netherlands in London in March 1824, resolving disputes left over from an earlier 1814 treaty.

aceh.name: Aceh
aceh.summary: Indonesia's westernmost province, on Sumatra, the only province with official Islamic law and a key point of entry for Islam's spread into Southeast Asia.

royal-netherlands-east-indies-army.name: Royal Netherlands East Indies Army
royal-netherlands-east-indies-army.summary: The military force the Kingdom of the Netherlands maintained in its colony of the Dutch East Indies, in what is now Indonesia.

dominique-lef-bvre.name: Dominique Lefèbvre
dominique-lef-bvre.summary: French missionary and bishop in Vietnam (1810 to 1865) whose two imprisonments under Emperor Thiệu Trị became a pretext for the first French naval interventions there.

thi-u-tr.name: Thiệu Trị
thi-u-tr.summary: Third emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty, reigning from 1841 until his death in 1847 as the eldest son and successor of Emperor Minh Mạng.

h-m-nghi.name: Hàm Nghi
h-m-nghi.summary: Eighth emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty (1871–1944), enthroned at age 12 in 1884 and remembered as a patriotic monarch for resisting French colonial rule before dying in exile in Algeria.

muong-people.name: Muong people
muong-people.summary: An ethnic group native to mountainous northern Vietnam, the country's third-largest minority with about 1.45 million people, speaking a language related to Vietnamese.

c-n-v-ng-movement.name: Cần Vương movement
c-n-v-ng-movement.summary: A large-scale Vietnamese insurgency (1885–1896) against French colonial rule, aiming to expel the French and restore deposed emperor Hàm Nghi; it lacked central coordination and faded out by 1889.

andrew-jackson.name: Andrew Jackson
andrew-jackson.summary: Seventh president of the United States (1829–1837), a former general whose political philosophy shaped Jacksonian democracy; a controversial figure over his policies toward Native Americans.

phan-nh-ph-ng.name: Phan Đình Phùng
phan-nh-ph-ng.summary: A Vietnamese revolutionary (died 1896) who led rebel armies against French colonial forces and was later hailed as a national hero for his uncompromising resistance.

ho-ng-hoa-th-m.name: Hoàng Hoa Thám
ho-ng-hoa-th-m.summary: Vietnamese feudal lord of Yên Thế (1858–1913) who led the Yên Thế Insurrection against the French protectorate in Tonkin for 30 years.

nguy-n-du.name: Nguyễn Du
nguy-n-du.summary: Poet and scholar-official (1766–1820) from a noble family who lived through the fall of three Vietnamese dynasties and is regarded as one of Vietnamese literature's most important writers.

the-tale-of-kieu.name: The Tale of Kiều
the-tale-of-kieu.summary: A Vietnamese epic poem of 3,254 verses by Nguyễn Du (1765–1820), recounting the hardships of Thúy Kiều, who sells herself into marriage to save her family; translated into 20 languages.

ch-n-m.name: Chữ Nôm
ch-n-m.summary: A complex writing system adapting Chinese characters to write vernacular Vietnamese, used mainly between the 15th and 19th centuries by literati such as Nguyễn Du.

gia-long.name: Gia Long
gia-long.summary: Born Nguyễn Phúc Ánh, he reunited Vietnam after civil war and became founding emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty in 1802, ruling until 1820.

jean-louis-taberd.name: Jean-Louis Taberd
jean-louis-taberd.summary: A French missionary (1794–1840) and Catholic bishop who compiled a Vietnamese dictionary building on earlier work by Pierre Pigneau de Béhaine.

vietnamese-alphabet.name: Vietnamese alphabet
vietnamese-alphabet.summary: The Latin-based writing system for Vietnamese, devised in the early 17th century by Portuguese missionary Francisco de Pina and other Jesuits, using diacritics to mark 29 letters and tones.

nguy-n-tr-ng-t.name: Nguyễn Trường Tộ
nguy-n-tr-ng-t.summary: Roman Catholic scholar and reformer (1830–1871) under Emperor Tự Đức who pushed for the modernisation of Vietnam and criticised the rigid Confucianism of the Huế court.

chulalongkorn.name: Chulalongkorn
chulalongkorn.summary: Fifth king of Siam of the Chakri dynasty, reigning 1868 to 1910, who modernized the country and secured its independence despite pressure from Britain and France.

mongkut.name: Mongkut
mongkut.summary: King of Siam from 1851 to 1868, known for modernizing reforms and scientific interests, including correctly predicting the total solar eclipse of 18 August 1868, later dubbed 'the King of Siam's eclipse.'

prachuap-khiri-khan-province.name: Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
prachuap-khiri-khan-province.summary: A western province of Thailand on the Malay Peninsula, about 240 km south of Bangkok, bordering Myanmar's Tanintharyi Region.

cinchona.name: Cinchona
cinchona.summary: A genus of Andean trees whose bark yields quinine, the main effective treatment for malaria during European colonialism until synthetic quinine appeared in 1944.

tonkin-free-school.name: Tonkin Free School
tonkin-free-school.summary: A short-lived school founded in Hanoi in 1907 that offered free classes in modern subjects to reform Vietnamese society under French rule, shut down within months.

siriraj-hospital.name: Siriraj Hospital
siriraj-hospital.summary: The oldest and largest public hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, and the primary teaching hospital of Mahidol University's Faculty of Medicine.

cochinchina-campaign.name: Cochinchina campaign
cochinchina-campaign.summary: A series of French and Spanish military operations from 1858 to 1862 against Vietnam that opened the French conquest of Vietnam and led to the colony of Cochinchina.

treaty-of-saigon-1862.name: Treaty of Saigon (1862)
treaty-of-saigon-1862.summary: 1862 treaty in which Emperor Tự Đức of the Nguyễn dynasty ceded Saigon and three southern Vietnamese provinces to France and Spain.

treaty-of-hu-1863.name: Treaty of Huế (1863)
treaty-of-hu-1863.summary: A treaty signed on 14 April 1863 between Đại Nam (Vietnam) and the French Empire.

annam-french-protectorate.name: Annam
annam-french-protectorate.summary: A French protectorate covering central Vietnam from 1883 to 1949, nominally ruled by the Vietnamese Nguyễn dynasty and later folded into French Indochina.

french-protectorate-of-cambodia.name: French protectorate of Cambodia
french-protectorate-of-cambodia.summary: The period of French colonial rule over Cambodia from 1863, part of French Indochina, lasting until full independence in 1953.

1893-franco-siamese-crisis.name: Franco-Siamese Crisis of 1893
1893-franco-siamese-crisis.summary: Conflict between France and Siam that ended when French gunboats blockaded Bangkok, forcing Siam to cede most of present-day Laos to French Indochina.

anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909.name: Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909
anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909.summary: An agreement signed in Bangkok in 1909 in which Siam gave up claims to several northern Malay states, fixing the modern Thailand–Malaysia border.

kinabureau.name: Kina Bureau
kinabureau.summary: A Dutch organization founded in 1913 that regulated the global trade in cinchona bark, the source of quinine, effectively creating a Dutch-Indonesian monopoly on anti-malaria medicine.

v-n-th-n-movement.name: Văn Thân movement
v-n-th-n-movement.summary: A 19th-century movement led by Confucian scholar-gentry in central Vietnam who opposed Western and Christian influence and sought to preserve Vietnamese tradition.

l-v-n-duy-t.name: Lê Văn Duyệt
l-v-n-duy-t.summary: Vietnamese general (1763/64–1832) who helped found the Nguyễn dynasty and later governed southern Vietnam as viceroy, clashing with Emperor Minh Mạng over his defence of Christian missionaries.

treaty-of-hu-1883.name: Treaty of Huế (1883)
treaty-of-hu-1883.summary: Also known as the Harmand Treaty, it was dictated by French administrator François-Jules Harmand after France seized the Thuận An forts in August 1883.

treaty-of-hu-1884.name: Treaty of Huế (1884)
treaty-of-hu-1884.summary: Also called the Patenôtre Treaty, it was negotiated by Jules Patenôtre and formed the basis of French colonial rule in Vietnam for seven decades, until the 1949 Élysée Accords.

townsend-harris.name: Townsend Harris
townsend-harris.summary: American merchant and politician (1804–1878), the first US Consul General to Japan, who negotiated the Harris Treaty opening Shogunate Japan to foreign trade.

o-b-u-s-n-k-h-ng.name: Đạo Bửu Sơn Kỳ Hương
o-b-u-s-n-k-h-ng.summary: A Vietnamese religious tradition meaning 'Way of the Strange Fragrance from the Precious Mountain,' first practiced by the mystic Đoàn Minh Huyên from 1849 and later continued by Huỳnh Phú Sổ, founder of the Hòa Hảo sect.

b-y-n-i.name: Bảy Núi (Thất Sơn)
b-y-n-i.summary: A range of small mountains, the "Seven Mountains," in southern Vietnam's An Giang Province near Cambodia, including the highest peak in the Mekong Delta.

conrad-malte-brun.name: Conrad Malte-Brun
conrad-malte-brun.summary: Dano-French geographer and journalist (1775–1826) credited with coining the names "Oceania" around 1812 and "Indo-China" in 1804.

malay-archipelago.name: Malay Archipelago
malay-archipelago.summary: Archipelago of over 25,000 islands between mainland Southeast Asia and Australia, the largest archipelago by area in the world, including Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.

east-indies.name: East Indies
east-indies.summary: An Age-of-Discovery term for lands around the Indian Ocean, most narrowly the Malay Archipelago now comprising Indonesia, New Guinea and the Philippines.

minh-h-ng.name: Minh Hương
minh-h-ng.summary: Descendants of Ming dynasty Chinese immigrants who settled in southern Vietnam during the 16th to 18th centuries, among the first ethnic Han to arrive there.
